precepts.text: Sufficient to such a man is this punishment: he got punished for his action because he was in error. Now contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him. Some brothers do not have the spirit to comfort; they look at the comfort part as weak. The Bible says forgive and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow: you never allow him to grow out of the situation, he feels repentance is hopeless, and you destroy a brother. Confirm your love toward him. It is not a weak nature to forgive a brother and confirm your love: I see you fighting, you are trying to get right, we are here for you. And do it lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices, and one of his devices is unforgiveness. If a brother has not committed the same infraction again, why do you keep bringing it up over and over? That is something you are battling.
precepts.point: Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing, lacking nothing.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.” Why count it joy? Because you are learning about yourself, what you have to fix. Some come to this truth and never knew they deal with a spirit of unforgiveness. They can’t let somebody off the hook for something that happened ten years ago, five years ago; they still harbor it. The word of God reveals it: I struggle with getting past things. Good, because now you can learn how to forgive, and you want forgiveness yourself. That is a trying of your faith, and Paul shows it in Corinthians.

“Sufficient to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many.” He got punished for his action because he was in error. “So that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him.” Contrariwise, the opposite side of his punishment: he paid it, now forgive him. Some brothers don’t have the spirit to comfort; they look at the comfort part as weak. Bro, the Bible says forgive and comfort him.

“lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.” If you don’t allow him or her to grow out of the situation, they feel it is hopeless, there is no chance to repent and get right, and you destroy a brother. “Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him.” It is not a weak nature to forgive a brother and confirm your love: it’s going to be all right, I see you fighting, you are trying to get right, we are here for you. Not babying him, but not holding him to something he moved on from.

“For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things.” He served his punishment; now let’s see the proof of you: can you forgive? “Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” One of his devices is unforgiveness. A brother who stole may not be let into your house again; that is not what this is about. But if he hasn’t committed the same infraction again, and you keep saying remember that time you stole, five years later, that is something you are battling within you, and Satan has you. Let patience have her perfect work, “that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.”

precepts.text: When I was yet young, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer; I prayed for her before the temple, and will seek her out even to the end. I directed my soul unto her, and I found her in pureness. You want to be tethered to wisdom because with wisdom you avoid the punishment. My heart was troubled in seeking her: because as you seek her, you start realizing the issues you have, the severity of what God is talking about. At first it sounds good, the fringes and the feast days; but now you are learning what you really are inside, a murmurer, a backbiter, and your heart is troubled. Therefore have I gotten a good possession.
precepts.point: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally. How do we ask of God? Do you think wisdom just floats down from heaven? No: you have to study, you have to open the book. And how do you know unless you have a teacher? Somebody has to teach you, and as you grow in understanding you realize, like Paul, I had not known sin but by the law. Now you know what you have to fix in you.

precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God.” How do we ask of God? Do you think wisdom just floats down from heaven? No. You have to study; you have to open the book. And how do you know unless you have a teacher? Somebody has to teach you. As you grow in understanding you realize, like Paul, an expert in the law, that you had not known sin but by the law: I didn't know this was covetousness. Now you know what you have to fix in you.

Ecclesiasticus shows the man who asked: “When I was yet young, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer. I prayed for her before the temple, and will seek her out even to the end.” He seeks wisdom to the end because wisdom will direct your path. “For thou savedst me from destruction, and deliveredst me from the evil time: therefore will I give thanks, and praise thee”: I will thank you because you will deliver me from that evil path.

“I directed my soul unto her, and I found her in pureness.” I redirected what I was doing and directed my soul to wisdom, because wisdom in its pureness will direct my path and save me. You want to be tethered to wisdom because with wisdom you avoid the punishment. That's what we all want: to get ourselves right, to be a better servant, a better husband, a better father. Teach me, God. Well, somebody has to teach you.

“I have had my heart joined with her from the beginning, therefore shall I not be forsaken. My heart was troubled in seeking her: therefore have I gotten a good possession.” As you seek her, you start realizing all the issues you have, and the severity of what God is talking about: eternal damnation, some learning it after death by pain. I can't get past this porn, I can't get past lying. At first it sounds good: I put on fringes, we keep the feast days, we turn up. But now I'm learning, damn, I'm a hateful ass brother, I'm a murmurer, I'm a backbiter. My heart is troubled.

Then: “Draw near unto me, ye unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.” You come to the house of learning, and somebody is going to teach you how to direct yourself. So now they're teaching you, and now you're mad? Do we understand what we signed up for? You said you wanted wisdom; here it is. No, you don't really want wisdom. You want church.

precepts.text: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts. You are asking God to measure you against his word. And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting. So when you ask God for wisdom and he starts showing you your errors, that is the prayer being answered. Blessed is the man that endures it.

Somebody has to teach you, and as you grow in understanding you realize, like Paul, I had not known sin but by the law. Now you know what you have to fix in you.

precepts.why:
If any man lack wisdom, let him ask of God: you pray, you ask of God, then you go to a house of learning and you learn. And what are you asking for? “Search me, O God, and know my heart”: know what I think, how I process your information. “try me, and know my thoughts”: I'm asking God to measure me against his word.

“And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.” Tell me, Lord, if there's any wicked way in me, and lead me in the right way. That's what we are all asking God to do: show us. So when you ask God for wisdom and he starts showing you your errors, that is the prayer being answered.

That's why James says, “My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.” You count it joy because you asked, show me all my wicked ways so I can fix them. “But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” You ask God to show you, the scripture comes correcting you, and now you're wavering. What are you doing when you waver? Trying to dodge correction.

So when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. It's not the sin a person commits so much as what they do afterwards that shows who they are, because none of us is right. Do they take their medicine, the scriptures? Big talk, and as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses. Blessed is the man that endures it: just listen, learn, and live.

precepts.text: Be not ashamed to confess thy sins, and force not the course of the river. The river is flowing, and you are trying to reroute it away from you. You are trying to dodge correction.
precepts.point: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways: always tossed around, never steady, never going head on.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” You ask God in faith to show you about you so you can fix you, knowing he will direct you on the right path. “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” Now you have asked God to show you, the scripture comes to you correcting, and you are wavering. What are you trying to do when you waver? You are trying to dodge correction.

Sirach says it: “Be not ashamed to confess thy sins; and force not the course of the river.” Here is the river, flowing. You are trying to reroute it away from you, trying to make it go another direction. You are dodging correction and making it seem like something it is not.

That is the double minded man, “unstable in all his ways”: always tossed around, forever moving, never straight, never steady, never going head on. With God “is no variableness”; with man there is variableness: jumping all over the place, can’t take it, making excuses, always responding, always having something to say, never listening. Some start answering before you can even finish the sentence; they are not listening to understand, they are listening to respond. A man of wisdom listens from a neutral position, takes in all the information, then discerns whether it fits him.

You said you wanted wisdom. Here it is. So don’t be ashamed to confess your sins, and don’t force the course of the river.

precepts.text: But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream. Let judgment run down. Do not waver and get around it; do not force the course to divert it.
precepts.point: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways: always tossed around, never steady, never going head on.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
The one who wavers is trying to dodge correction, to force the course of the river. Amos shows the river as it should flow: “But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.”

That is a river. Let judgment run down as waters. Let it run. Don’t waver and try to get around it; don’t try to force the course to divert it. Let judgment come down, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

You asked God to show you your errors, and he is showing you. “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed. For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.” If you keep rerouting the judgment away from yourself, you will not receive the wisdom you asked for. Let it run down on you, accept it, and fix what it shows you.

precepts.text: I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him. That is taking accountability. Until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he shall bring me forth to the light. Why? Because I do not dodge what I asked for. I asked God to show me my secret faults, and now that he is showing me, this is not the time to start dodging, making excuses, or blaming the brothers for not checking in on me. Take your medicine and move on. I do not judge a person by the infraction so much as by what they do afterwards: do they take their medicine, the scriptures? Big talk means nothing if you ghost as soon as correction comes.
precepts.point: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways: always tossed around, never steady, never going head on.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him.” What is that person saying? He is taking accountability: I will bear the judgment of God, because I have sinned. “until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.”

Don’t try to get around the cause. Don’t try to deviate from the judgment. Don’t make excuses. Stop wavering. You asked God to show you, he has shown you where you are wrong, and now you are trying to bypass it: maybe I would be better if you brothers called me and checked in on me; it’s your fault. Do you think this is Disney and this is a ride? You can ride that pony by yourself.

Why will he bring me forth to the light? Because I don’t dodge what I asked for. I asked God to show me my secret faults and my errors because I want to get better, and now that he is showing me, this is not the time to start dodging. We all fall short.

How do you endure in the truth? Listen, learn and live. There is no special recipe: when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. As soon as the medicine comes, people start running. The infraction does not tell who a person is so much as what they do afterwards: do they take their medicine, the scriptures? If they can’t, they lose respect. All the big words mean nothing if, as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses because of pride and ego.

precepts.text: Precept brought by the captain: I brought this people out of bondage, and gave them my commandments by my servants the prophets, whom they would not hear, but despised my counsels. The counsel the prophets bring out of the scriptures is God's counsel; when you resist it, it is not men you are despising. The carnal man causes you to resist the direction God wants you to grow in.
precepts.point: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways: always tossed around, never steady, never going head on.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
When people come into this faith, the challenge is dealing with the spiritual man as opposed to the carnal man. They pray for wisdom, for discernment, to grow in the truth, and then they will not listen to the men appointed before them, because the carnal man or carnal woman does not see things spiritually. Ezra shows the spirit behind it: “Thus saith the Lord, I brought this people out of bondage, and I gave them my commandments by menservants the prophets; whom they would not hear, but despised my counsels.”

God gave his commandments by the prophets to teach the people, and they would not hear the prophets. But whose counsels did they despise? “my counsels”: God’s. The prophets open the scriptures and show you thus saith the Lord to help you overcome what you are dealing with, and when you resist, it is the counsel God truly gave you that you despise. It came through men, but God inspired it.

So whoever brings correction your way, men or women, it is for your benefit, and they are being inspired by the Lord to direct you according to the path you should walk. Be humble, be quiet and listen. They are coming out of the scriptures and showing your error. Learn; this is how we grow. The carnal man will cause you to resist the direction God wants you to grow in, and that is the wavering, double minded man who shall not receive any thing of the Lord.

All scripture is given by inspiration of God for reproof, correction and instruction in righteousness. It is not a book to tote your ego so you feel good. If the Lord showed us who we are, we would be ashamed; it is only the mercy of Christ and his promise that we are here. For us to change, somebody has to tell us what we were doing wrong, and when they do, don’t get mad.

precepts.text: I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men. That goes with Deuteronomy 28:64: scattered and serving gods of wood and stone, we were spotted. James writes to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, ones that had been living as sinners. So count it joy when God starts showing you who you are.
precepts.point: Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures. The literal firstfruits brought to God had to be without spot. We are supposed to keep ourselves unspotted from the world; and to become unspotted, we have to learn what we were doing wrong so we can fix it. So why are you mad? That is the whole purpose.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” We were formed in his image, in his likeness, to be righteous. The literal firstfruits given to God had to be perfect; an animal could not be spotted. And James says pure religion is “to keep himself unspotted from the world.” But we all fall short.

So who is James writing to? “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. Moses said it: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. The Most High scattered us and made our remembrance cease. That goes with Deuteronomy 28:64, where we are scattered and serve gods of wood and stone. When we were serving gods of wood and stone, we were spotted.

So James is writing to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, ones that were living as sinners. Count it joy when God starts showing you who you are. To live an unspotted life, we have to learn what we were doing wrong so we can fix it. So why are you mad? That is the whole purpose. God sends teachers to show us how to get right; we get cleansed because we are swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.

And once we are unspotted, we go out and help others the same way: to visit “the fatherless and widows in their affliction”, the ones with no guide, no hedge, nobody to lead them, so they can become unspotted too. The scattered, forgotten tribes are the firstfruits God begat with the word of truth, and the good and perfect gift from above is the wisdom that makes us clean again.

precepts.text: Submit yourselves therefore to God: take the counsel. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. How do you resist him? By submitting to God first. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. How do you draw nigh? You come to the house of learning, somebody teaches you, and God draws nigh back to you and gives you a way to escape. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
precepts.point: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life. How do you know what you can endure unless you go through it? You do not know if you can lift the weight until it is on the rack. You are asking for muscles; well, you have to lift.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God.” You want to blame somebody: Lord, it ain’t me, you put that big booty woman in front of me. The Lord says stop, bro. I put the nine millimeter in front of you, but you didn’t shoot yourself; I put the knife in your hand; I put the crack pipe in the room, but you didn’t smoke it. “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed is when something appeals to you and you give in; you entertain it. That is on you; that is your choice. God is just showing you what your vice is, and now that is what you are fighting.

When you are tempted, you are supposed to resist. James tells how: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” Submit yourself to God: take the counsel. How do you resist the devil? By first submitting yourself to God.

“Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.” How are you going to draw nigh to God? Somebody is going to teach you and you are going to learn; you go to the house of learning. That is what you are doing now. And God will draw nigh to you and give you a way to escape. “Blessed is the man that endureth temptation.” How do you know what you can endure unless you go through it? You don’t know you can bench 315 until it is on the rack. You are asking for muscles; you have to lift.

“Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” We just read that in chapter one: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” Now that you hear the correction about how to get right with God, you have excuses. You see the sin in front of you and turn away, like seeing a booger in your nose in the mirror and turning your head; the booger is still there. “receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls. But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only.” The glass is the Bible; you see yourself in it and walk away and forget. You can close the book; you are still a sinner. Submit, resist, draw nigh, and cleanse your hands.

precepts.text: James writes to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad. Would it be a surprise for us to be called Greeks and barbarians? We were scattered abroad throughout the four corners of the earth.
precepts.point: Book read in class: Israel Redivivus, being a history of the tribes of Israel distinct from that of Judah, by Frederick Charles Danvers: with regard to the Israelites, it must be remembered that each tribe was divided into different families or subtribes, even as there were at a later date many tribes bearing different names who were collectively known to the Greeks as Scythians. The Scythians were nomadic people of that area. We were scattered everywhere, so we are the Barbarians, we are the Scythians, we are the Greeks. This is our book.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“Where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free.” A Christian will say, to hell with all the facts you just showed, because Greeks, Barbarians and Scythians are the other nations. Really, after reading all of that in context? No.

A history of the Jewish diaspora shows that the Jews in the western diaspora basically knew only Greek; their Torah reading and prayer were conducted in Greek, and the scripture was translated into Greek for those communities. So some of our people were called Greeks and some were called Jews, a language difference, but the same people. Barbarian comes from the Greek barbaros, what the early Greeks called all foreigners, including the Romans.

James writes “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” Would it be a surprise for us to be called Greeks and barbarians? We were scattered abroad throughout the four corners of the earth, and Esau with his demonic self has tried to insert himself in our place.

Israel Redivivus by Frederick Charles Danvers says each tribe was divided into families and subtribes, and later many tribes bearing different names were known collectively to the Greeks as Scythians, the nomadic people of that area. We were scattered everywhere, so we are the Barbarians, we are the Scythians, we are the Greeks. Get mad; this is our book.

precepts.text: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. You are going to be tempted by Satan; he is going to use devices to tempt you. Set thy heart aright: get your mind right, get yourself together, because this is not going to be a fair fight. And constantly endure: you have to constantly endure these temptations, because you have things in you that you need to purge off, and some of these things keep coming back. That is why Paul in Romans 7 asked the Lord to take the thorn away, and the Lord said no, this is what you are going to have to battle. But on the flip side, dealing with those battles is what keeps us going in this truth: always trying to get better with our life, how we communicate, how we deal in relationships, how we deal with one another. Make not haste in time of trouble: things are going to happen and you cannot fold up; you have to fight. Everybody is not going to make it victorious. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate: for gold is tried in the fire. You are going to be tried, so make sure you are on point.
precepts.point: And sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death. It becomes action; that sin is the action you take after you have been enticed by your lust. And it always ends in destruction. That is why we have to be on point.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life.” You are going to be tried. Sirach tells you to get ready for it: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” You are going to be tempted by Satan; he is going to use devices to tempt you.

“Set thy heart aright”: get your damn mind right, get yourself together, because this is not going to be a fair fight, and it is not going to be easy. “and constantly endure”: you have to constantly endure these temptations, because you have demons in you that you need to purge off, and some of these things keep coming back, and you have to be able to fight and get away from them. Paul in Romans 7 asked the Lord to take it away, and the Lord said no, this is the thorn in your side; this is what you will have to battle. But on the flip side, dealing with those battles is what keeps us going in this truth: always trying to get better with our lives, how we communicate, how we deal in relationships and with one another.

“and make not haste in time of trouble.” Things are going to happen, and you can’t fold up; go full-fledged toward it and knock it out. Life is a fight, and everybody is not going to make it victorious and on top. “Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate. For gold is tried in the fire.”

You are going to be tried, so make sure you are on point. Everything in the world is against the person trying to be righteous: the work schedule set up to keep you in sin on the weekend, the holidays you want off based on wickedness. So you have to be around righteous people who will hold you accountable. That is the man who endures temptation and receives the crown of life.

precepts.text: In the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits. A seducing spirit looks like it is good for you, but it is going to destroy you; like drugs: that crack feels real good, but you are not able to see around you, and your whole life is being destroyed. That is why it is important to be studying, reading your four chapters, being around godly men and godly women, so somebody can have your back.
precepts.point: And sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death. It becomes action; that sin is the action you take after you have been enticed by your lust. And it always ends in destruction. That is why we have to be on point.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed means there is some attraction there, something that makes us gravitate toward the elements in us that cause us to sin. It seduces us: it looks like it is right for us, but it is not. Paul warned of it: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits.”

A seducing spirit looks like it is good for you, but it is going to destroy you. Like drugs: that crack feels real good to the crackhead, but he is not able to see around him, and his whole life is being destroyed.

The only way you are going to see whether it is good for you or not is by filtering it through the scriptures. That is why it is important to be studying, reading your four chapters, being around godly men and godly women, so somebody can have your back. You have to be in the spirit to discern whether a thing is righteousness or Satan’s kiss.

Temptation begins internally; the lust is in you. When temptation presents itself you begin to be drawn to it, sin starts enticing you, and it grows through agreement: you get enticed, then you agree with it. “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” It becomes action, and it always ends in destruction. “There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.” In your own counsel you will always think you are right, and that is how people give heed to seducing spirits and depart from the faith.

precepts.text: Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.
precepts.point: The feast of firstfruits: count seven sabbaths complete from the wave offering, and number fifty days. Seven sabbaths again, complete.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
James says it the same way: “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.”

The Most High, of his own will, begat us with the word of truth for this purpose, that we should be a kind of firstfruits. We become that if we follow after Christ’s example, since Christ is the firstfruits risen from the dead.

So the feast of firstfruits in Leviticus 23:15-17, the new offering brought to the Lord after seven sabbaths complete, is a picture of Christ and of the people he begets by the word: the best of the best, offered unto the Lord.

precepts.text: Lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls. But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves: we hear the class about putting away all bitterness, and then do not do it. That is the man beholding his natural face in a glass who goeth his way and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was. We do not want that: we want to examine ourselves and say, Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit.
precepts.point: And be not conformed to this world: why? Because of who rules over this world. Do not take the mind of Cain. But be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind: after Christ; that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
James tells us what to put off and what to take in: “Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” The word received with meekness is what saves the soul.

“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” We have to be doers of the word, family. We hear the class about putting away all bitterness, and then we don't do it.

“For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.” When you read the scriptures, you see yourself in them. But after you read them, you go your way and don't really address the matter.

We don't want to do that. We want to examine ourselves, look to the scriptures and say: Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit. I'm bitter toward my wife, I'm bitter toward the leadership, I'm bitter toward my brother. We have to confess that thing and pray to the Lord to remove that spirit from us. That is being transformed by the renewing of the mind, and not conformed to this world.

precepts.text: Whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart. That is exactly how lust is conceived: it starts with the look, and then the thought, in your heart, before anything physical ever happens.
precepts.point: And sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death. Some of you say, I fornicated and I did not die. That death is talking about damnation, your soul being destroyed. God will judge you.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

precepts.why:
“Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin.” Where is lust conceived? In your mind; that is where the root begins. Christ shows exactly how: “But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” That is how lust is conceived.

We are living in an evil world, and we all see beautiful women. A picture of an immodestly dressed woman was put on the screen and the brothers were asked one by one what they saw. One liked the way she dressed. Another said she is beautiful, but the way she dresses you have to hate that thing, she has to be modest. Another said, I have been in the world a lot longer than in the truth, so I am working on hating it. What you see on the screen you see every damn day when you go outside, and some of you break your neck walking down the street.

You have to train yourself to hate evil. It doesn’t come naturally; you cannot come to the truth and all of a sudden hate what you see out there. When you see her, train your mind: she has AIDS, she stinks, she has to be a man. If you don’t, you will always be watching and desiring these things. Older brothers with experience have matured past it; the young brothers dealing with youthful lusts have to train. Sisters, before the truth many of you walked around in miniskirts and spandex, giggling and giving out your number to every dude on the block, and now you have changed how you dress. When Christ returns there will be a modesty law set up.

So you see it, and in your mind you say, damn, I don’t mind sleeping with that. When you allow that thought, lust is conceived, and sin comes forth. But if the thought comes and you shake it off, what’s wrong with you, God is going to kill you, stop thinking like that, it is not conceived. If you sit down and entertain it, it brings forth sin. That is why Christ says adultery doesn’t start when you literally lie down with a woman; it starts in your mind. “and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” Some say I fornicated and I didn’t die; that death is damnation, your soul being destroyed. God will judge you.

precepts.text: To the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad.
precepts.point: Among the heathen they profaned his holy name when men said of them, these are the people of the Lord and are gone forth out of his land: the real black Jews telling the white man you are the Jews, God's chosen people, is that prophecy today.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
Ezekiel tells why the real 12 tribes were removed: “when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it by their own way and by their doings: their way was before me as the uncleanness of a removed woman.” We defiled our land by our own ways, like a menstruous woman; that is how disgusted God was with us, and he had to remove us out of the land. “Wherefore I poured my fury upon them for the blood that they had shed upon the land, and for their idols wherewith they had polluted it: And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries”.

James writes to that same people: “James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” The New Testament letter is addressed to the 12 tribes, scattered abroad, exactly as Ezekiel said they would be. I don't know why a Christian can't understand this.

And once scattered, “when they entered unto the heathen, whither they went, they profaned my holy name, when they said to them, These are the people of the Lord, and are gone forth out of his land.” How do we profane God's holy name? We started to say, y'all are the Jews now, we're not the Jews. We started to call the white man Jews. So that is the prophecy of what is going on today: the real black Jews saying to the white man, y'all are the Jews, y'all are God's chosen people.

So the real Israel is the people scattered among the nations, the twelve tribes James wrote to, not the ones who took the land with despiteful minds and called their European friends to come and get a part of it.

precepts.text: Every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed. The temptation comes from something already within you. If you have a problem with wanting to be the head, wanting to be the shot caller in the home, Satan plays with that, and you will look up and there will be a complete role reversal in your home.
precepts.point: A lot of sisters forget it is the house of the man. Joshua said, As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord; he did not say, As for me and my house in agreement with my wife. He commanded his home. That is the natural place and position of a man. And some brothers remove themselves from it: you want to be a mama's boy in your marriage, you want her to mother you instead of you leading her, and that emboldens her; now you are her child, and that is how she speaks to you.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
Paul fears “lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted”. Satan is able to see what is within you, and that is what he attacks: not the stuff you are strong in, but the stuff you are weak in. “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” The temptation comes from something already within you.

So if you have a problem with wanting to be the head honcho, wanting to be over your husband, wanting to be the shot caller in control of how things go in the home, Satan plays with that, and you will look up and there will be a complete role reversal in your home. Subtle means pleasing to the senses in a mild or nuanced way. That little bit of power feels good: I decide what we eat around here, I put up the curtains, I picked this out. Then you start overstepping your bounds and do not even know it was Satan who set you up with the curtains. Sisters, when you start to overstep your divine place and purpose, say, that's Satan, you almost got me.

Most of us have been infected by the westernized mindset: birthdays, baby showers, Mother's Day and Father's Day, Thanksgiving, the ring on the finger, rules God did not make that we think are how life is supposed to be. The same goes for how a man deals with his wife. A father who told his son, get your money, the hoes are going to come, and left a condom on his dresser for him, normalized it. That residue has to be let go completely, or it will cloud your judgment and ruin your marriage.

It is the house of the man. Joshua said, as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord; he did not say, in agreement with my wife. He commanded his home. And some brothers take themselves out of that role and want to be a mama's boy in the marriage, wanting her to mother them instead of leading her. That emboldens her, and now you are her child and that is how she speaks to you. Both are drawn away by their own lust, and Satan works subtly on what is already within.

precepts.text: A double-minded man is unstable in all his ways: you hear it in his speech and daily decisions, and he is not ready to be hopped behind.
precepts.point: Never aim down spiritually: a sister of years teaching a novice husband to wear his fringes daily will lose respect for him and go elsewhere for understanding, and that is marrying down.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

precepts.why:
James puts it in one line: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” That is the man of Proverbs 25:28, the man who “hath no rule over his own spirit”, a city “broken down, and without walls.” He is cast about, blown to and fro with every wind of doctrine, and a double mind is what keeps him unstable.

Sisters, these are the things to look for. You see the signs. You hear it in his speech and in his daily decision-making. He doesn't know if he is coming or going: one minute it's this, the next minute it's that. He has something brand new he is trying to bring out, like mashed potatoes on the Passover, and you know it did not come from leadership. Red flag. And when he fixes it, sister, you better run.

This is the man you are going to hop behind and expect to make sure everything is taken care of? You mess around and be homeless, trying to figure it out. He is not ready yet. He is unstable.

So when looking for a husband, ask: does this man have stability, does he have discipline? A man with no rule over his spirit is not mentally sound, and he cannot take care of you. Aim up, never down: look for a man with more understanding than you, who can lead you and guide you.

precepts.text: Pure religion undefiled is to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction and to keep himself unspotted from the world. You keep yourself unspotted by tethering to the wisdom flowing down from God, not by trying to sleep with the sister who just came out of the world.
precepts.point: In all ages she enters holy souls and makes them friends of God and prophets. She cannot dwell in a body subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness, or hatred. When you move like that you start saying absurd things. A prophet's job is to raise up God's children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:26: “For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness.” Wisdom is unspotted. James 1:27 shows how a man keeps himself the same way.

“Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.”

You keep yourself unspotted from the world by visiting the fatherless and the afflicted, all people afflicted in the mind. But you are too busy trying to bag the chick. She came out of the world, out of whatever she was doing, and instead of leading her to God you are trying to sleep with her.

If we want to know how to keep ourselves unspotted, we tether ourselves to God, because flowing down from him is wisdom. You come into this truth not knowing any better, wisdom flows down from God to you, you apply it, and you become new: “she maketh all things new.”

precepts.text: Receive with meekness the engrafted word, the law and the testimony, which is able to save your soul, and be ye doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves like the man who forgets his face in the glass and goes back to sin. Whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty and continueth, a doer of the work, shall be blessed in his deed.
precepts.point: The same Paul who said no man is justified by the works of the law says not the hearers of the law are just before God but the doers of the law shall be justified. Was he schizophrenic? No; the law in Galatians is sacrifice, elaborated in Hebrews 7, 9 and 10, and the law here is the commandments, and faith comes first and the works follow.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
In Galatians Paul says you are not justified by the works of the law, and Christians say, see, we don’t have to keep the commandments; Christ died for us, just believe. Then the same Paul writes, “For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.” Was Paul schizophrenic? No. The law in Galatians is animal sacrifice, explained in Hebrews 7, 9 and 10, which Christ did away with. The law here is the commandments. Faith comes first, and then the works follow.

Christ’s brother James answers the same way: “Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness”: lay aside all sin. “And receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” The engrafted word is the law and the testimony. Some heard in church that the law cannot save you, only Christ can. The law in Christ saves you; keeping God’s commandments can save your soul.

“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” That takes you right back to Romans 2:13. Christianity tells you that you do not have to keep God’s commandments and will still be saved; they deceive themselves and others. “For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.” He reads the Bible, says yeah okay, and goes back to sinning, looking in the mirror and forgetting what he saw.

“But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.” The work is the commandments; blessed in his deed is justified. Christ gave us liberty from the law of sin and death, the sacrifices under which a man “died without mercy”, but that liberty is not freedom from doing the commandments. The doers of the law shall be justified.

precepts.text: James, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad. If Revelation 7:9 confounds you on the street, shame on you.
precepts.point: When thou art in tribulation and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord and be obedient, he is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee nor destroy thee, the lake of fire, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers. That is the crown of life of Revelation 2:10.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” James wrote his letter to the twelve tribes, and he says where they are: scattered abroad. The scattering Moses prophesied in Deuteronomy 4:27 had already come upon them, and the apostles were writing to Israel in the nations.

It stands with Ezekiel 28:25, read in the same moment: “When I shall have gathered the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered, and shall be sanctified in them in the sight of the heathen, then shall they dwell in their land that I have given to my servant Jacob.” Israel is scattered among the people, and the Lord gathers Israel out of them back to the land he gave Jacob.

So the great multitude out of all nations in Revelation 7:9 is the twelve tribes scattered abroad, gathered back. This is what you say when they try to tell you on the street that people coming out of all nations means all peoples. If you let them confound you with Revelation 7:9, shame on you.

precepts.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, but let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. Sirach 4:17-18: at first wisdom walks with him by crooked ways, brings fear and dread, torments him with her discipline until she may trust his soul, then returns the straight way, comforts him, and shows him her secrets. There is no cap on wisdom. Hebrews 11:6, without faith it is impossible to please him, and Romans 10:17, faith cometh by hearing the word of God, so increase your study.
precepts.point: Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” If we lack wisdom, go to the source: go to the Father in the name of the Son, Jesus the Christ.

Sirach shows how wisdom deals with the one who seeks her: “For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws.” When we come into this truth we are not right, so wisdom walks with us in our crooked ways, and the Lord will jack us up because we are not doing it right; but wisdom will still be there. “Then will she return the straight way unto him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets.” There is no cap on wisdom.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” That is the key: you have to believe. “But without faith it is impossible to please him”. Without Christ it is impossible to please the Father, so we must build our faith. And “faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” We have to increase our study as we see the days approaching, and continue to converse in the scriptures.

precepts.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, in faith, nothing wavering; a double-minded man is unstable in all his ways. Some cannot discern why an adulterer was put out of the school. Pray for wisdom and discernment, but give the Lord something to work with: 2 Esdras 14:40, when Ezra drank, wisdom grew and his spirit strengthened his memory, because the Spirit needed a memory to access to rewrite the books. If the Bible is closed six days a week there is nothing in there for the Spirit to bring to mind. Views peak on Sabbath and nobody watches the rest of the week, the same as Christians on Sunday; many are called, few are chosen. Let the brother of low degree rejoice that he is exalted: the quiet brother who studies and prays becomes the one breaking down scripture years later. Sirach 11:12, the slow man wanting ability, the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good and set him up from his low estate. Put on Bible audio at night if reading hurts your eyes.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” If any of you are dumb as a rock, ask of God. Some do not have the spirit of discernment: they see right and wrong in front of them and cannot discern it. When judgment is passed there is always that one who asks why a brother or sister had to be put out of the school when all they did was commit a little adultery. Shut up and sit down; they cannot discern. So pray, as Hezekiah laid his prayer before the Lord: pray for wisdom, knowledge and the spirit of discernment.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” And give the Lord something to work with. You cannot sit at the table with a chicken leg in one hand and a steak in the other praying, Lord, help me lose weight. Likewise you pray for wisdom but the Bible is closed Sunday through Friday and opened only on the Sabbath. The views on the classes peak on Saturday and nobody watches the rest of the week, the same as Christians on Sunday. Many are called, few are chosen; this is for the chosen few that know what to do.

“For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways”: not some of his ways, all of them. Reading once a week leaves nothing for the Lord to work with.

“Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted.” That brother is studying, reading and praying, Lord help my understanding, even when he does not understand yet. The quiet brother who did not do much talking years back becomes the one breaking down what the scriptures mean. If reading hurts your eyes, put on Bible audio at night and wake up to the scriptures.

precepts.text: Out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness and the rest; they come from within and defile the man.
precepts.point: Every man is tempted when he is drawn away of his own lust and enticed. Lust has nothing to do with love.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Lust has nothing to do with love, and love has nothing to do with lust; a lot of us get those two confused. What is a man’s own lust? Christ shows it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.”

Read on: “Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” Adultery and fornication are sins we battle every day. The spirit of murder you see in this world, and our people fight that demon every day. Covetousness we fight every day, because we lust and covet after these things. Deceit is a demon we fight every day.

These come from within. So the battle is not really from the outside; the thing we lust after is within us, and the battlefield is the mind. A brother can be quiet here but fighting major demons; a sister can be quiet but fighting demons. Quiet does not mean humble. Some are bound with their sin.

And this world feeds it. Everything here is a work of sin. They sell sex everywhere; you think you are watching a movie or a karate flick, and they put that nasty thing in there, and down the line you see how people turn to watching porn. The devil is always there, pushing sin. That is why we have to understand this walk and overcome it: every man is drawn away of his own lust, the evil that comes from within his heart.

precepts.text: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; meditate therein day and night.
precepts.point: Whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty and continueth therein, a doer of the work, shall be blessed in his deed. Christ's grace is the platform to build on, so there is no going backwards.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
James says the blessed man is the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues therein, “not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work”. Joshua says the same thing another way: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night”.

Ask yourself, brothers and sisters: are you meditating in this book they call the Bible? Don't lie to yourself. If you have to ask, it means you need to do it more, because it is supposed to be a natural thing.

Why meditate on it day and night? Because we want to keep the ministry blameless, and because we know the job of Satan: he is like a roaring lion, waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments. When you meditate on something day and night, you have no time for foolishness. It is like the scriptures warning not to be idle, because when you are idle you fall back into sin. When you are constantly in the scriptures, your mind is focused on keeping the commandments. That is the pattern: stay focused.

The enemy is at work every day. Turn off the TV and the phone and you might have a two or three percent upper hand, but as long as these devices and human beings exist on this earth, our battle is serious and we are battling every day.

Joshua goes on: “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous”. That is James 1:25 again. The perfect law of liberty is what we look into: the commandments, the mercy of God, the grace of God. Christ died on the cross and gave us that grace as the platform to build upon, so we can no longer go backwards; now we have to go forward. The one who is not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work “shall be blessed in his deed”, blessed in his teaching and his business, whatever he does.

precepts.text: Your adversary the devil walketh about as a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
precepts.point: Whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty and continueth therein, a doer of the work, shall be blessed in his deed. Christ's grace is the platform to build on, so there is no going backwards.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
Why do we have to keep the book of the law in our mouth and meditate on it day and night? Because of the work of Satan. Peter shows it: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

Your adversary doesn't sleep. You think Satan sleeps for a minute? He does not sleep, brothers. When you know the enemy and know his job, you understand the scripture more. The book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth because Satan is like a devouring lion waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments.

James 1:14 already showed where the fight is: “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” When you are drawn away of your own lust, you are not in control; the lust is in control of you. So take every little thing as a big thing, because Satan is well alive here.

That is why the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty must continue therein, not a forgetful hearer but a doer. It is easy for us to go left, so we have to constantly put ourselves in the works. Either you are about it or you are not, and you cannot just be cool to everything while the lion is walking about.

precepts.text: The accuser of our brethren accused them before our God day and night.
precepts.point: Whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty and continueth therein, a doer of the work, shall be blessed in his deed. Christ's grace is the platform to build on, so there is no going backwards.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
The enemy does not sleep, and Revelation shows what he is doing: “And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.”

Satan isn't sleeping day and night. He is accusing us day and night as we study, trying to accuse us before the Lord. So we don't have time to be idle. We have to keep our minds focused, brothers. Y'all sleep on the devil if you want.

He is at work through this world too. They are trying to change times and laws and make people think that what is immoral is moral. The mind of the sinner says don't judge me and don't snitch, but the one living in sin influences others and destroys others. That is why the laws of God are important.

This is why James 1:25 calls us to look into the perfect law of liberty and continue therein. The accuser works against us before God day and night, so we must meditate in the law day and night and be doers of the work, so that we are blessed in our deed and the ministry stays blameless.

precepts.text: Be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves; it is applying what you heard that saves your soul, not attendance.
precepts.point: That thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: the end goal of talking about the commandments and meditating on the commandments is to do the commandments. Attending every class, hearing every breakdown, and keeping every precept list is all in vain if you never do thus saith the Lord; not doing the word of God is why we went into slavery and sit at the bottom of society.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” It is applying what you heard that saves your soul, not attendance. Hearers only are deceiving their own selves.

The third step of the formula is “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein”. Not doing the word of God is why we went into slavery and sit at the bottom of society. Be a doer.

precepts.text: Whoever lacks wisdom may ask of God, who gives to all men liberally, and it shall be given.
precepts.point: Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Most High, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel. Preparing the heart means setting the mind and spirit in order, examining oneself, and putting away the weak nature of sin before teaching others.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

precepts.why:
Ezra's skill in the law was not his own. “If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.”

Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law, and the understanding to teach statutes and judgments in Israel was given him by the good hand of his God. Whoever lacks wisdom today may do the same: ask of God, who gives to all men liberally and does not upbraid, and it shall be given.

precepts.text: Lacking wisdom, one may ask of God, who gives liberally, and it shall be given.
precepts.point: Ezra was ashamed to require of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help against the enemy in the way, having testified that the hand of God is upon all who seek him for good.

note.label: Ezra 8: The Company Returns And Fasts At Ahava

precepts.why:
Ezra fasted to seek of God “a right way for us.” That is asking for wisdom, and “If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.”

Ezra had told the king that “The hand of our God is upon all them for good that seek him”, and was ashamed to ask for soldiers and horsemen after saying so. So instead of the king's band he sought the Most High by fasting and prayer for a right path for the people, the little ones and their substance. Whoever lacks wisdom may ask the same way, and it shall be given.

precepts.text: Be doers of the word and not hearers only.
precepts.point: The covenant is to such as keep His commandments and remember them to do them. To do them is an action word.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
The mercy of the Lord is “To such as keep his covenant, and to those that remember his commandments to do them.” To do them is an action word.

James says the same: “But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” Be doers of the word and not hearers only. The man who only hears the commandments and does not do them is deceiving himself.

The covenant is to such as keep his commandments and remember them to do them. That is the doer of the word, and the mercy from everlasting to everlasting is on him.

precepts.point: When we read our four chapters we should read to understand, seeing how the examples of our forefathers and foremothers can be used for us.

David cried to his refuge and his portion in the land of the living, trusting the Most High to deal bountifully with him.

When we read our four chapters we should read to understand, seeing how the examples of our forefathers and foremothers can be used for us.

precepts.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad. The letter names who it is written to.
precepts.point: Israel was scattered among the nations, so Israel is in the nations. The one the Lord shakes his hand at is the heathen, so the heathen are not who is being joined to him here.

note.label: Zechariah 2: The Measuring Line and the Apple of His Eye

precepts.why:
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” The letter names who it is written to: the twelve tribes scattered abroad.

Israel is in the nations. So the many nations joined to the Lord in that day are his people coming out of the nations where they are scattered, not the heathen he shakes his hand at.

precepts.text: James writes "to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad," so all twelve tribes are still in view, not three tribes only.
precepts.point: There was an order and prophecy for the twelve tribes to be redeemed. The gospel went first to the southern kingdom, Judah, Benjamin, and Levi, the "Jews," and the "Jew and Gentile" and "Jew and Greek" language is the split between the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom of Israel, not Israel and the nations. The Most High did not cast away the northern tribes; the whole twelve tribes are scattered and being saved.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
James writes “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. All twelve tribes are still in view, not three tribes only.

The Most High did not cast away the northern tribes. The Jew and Gentile and Jew and Greek language is the split between the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom of Israel, not Israel and the nations. Judah is first, and the whole twelve tribes are scattered and being saved.

precepts.text: Written to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, showing "that nation" and the scattered children of God are the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles.
precepts.point: Caiaphas prophesied that one man should die for the people, speaking not of himself but from the prophecies he knew in Isaiah 53 and the Psalms. That nation he must die for is Israel, and "not for that nation only" means Christ would also gather the children of God scattered abroad, the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles the Christians claim.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
James writes “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”.

That nation Christ died for, and the children of God scattered abroad that he gathers in one, are the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles. The scattered ones are Israel, and the letters of the apostles went to them.

precepts.text: James writes to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad among the heathen.
precepts.point: It says "the Jew first, and also the Gentile" because prophecy set Judah, Benjamin, and Levi to rise up first, and the "Gentiles" are the dispersed northern tribes scattered among the heathen, left few in number. This is the diaspora, the same scattering some now call the African diaspora.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.”

James writes to the twelve tribes scattered abroad among the heathen. That is the “every nation” of Peter's word: not every race, but every nation where Israel was scattered.

precepts.text: James writes to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, the same scattered nation Peter and Paul addressed.
precepts.point: "But in every nation he that feareth him and worketh righteousness is accepted with him." The "every nation" is not the Chinese, Japanese, East Indian, or Caucasian; it is every nation into which the Israelites were scattered for disobedience.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.”

James writes to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, the same scattered nation Peter and Paul addressed. The Gentiles who received the word were of these tribes.

precepts.point: The circumcision was the southern kingdom of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi. The uncircumcised were primarily the northern kingdom.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.”

The twelve tribes were scattered abroad throughout all nations, starting from the Assyrian captivity onward. So when Peter says “in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him”, the word sent to the children of Israel finds them in every nation. Cornelius was one of the scattered, and the Gentiles of Paul's ministry are the tribes scattered abroad.
